an4.30:8.2: This pair is also mentioned in the same way regarding different teachings at [mn117:38.1]() and [sn22.62:13.2](). Nothing is known of them apart from these passages. It is likely that the current discourse is the original context, as it has a satisfying overall form, lacking in MN 117 and SN 22.62. The Buddha visits the wanderer’s monastery, where he engages them on a topic of fundamental principles that they should all share. Finally he points to ancient teachers who shared the same principles. | The text does not say that Vassa and Bhañña were wanderers. _Paribbājakā_ here is a vocative, as in the previous line, and as consistently at this point in this phrase ([mn51:3.2](), [mn117:38.1](), [an4.21:8.4](), etc.). | Ukkalā lay on the Bay of Bengal in the region today called Odisha. It was the origin of the merchants Tapussa and Bhallika who offered the first meal to the Buddha ([pli-tv-kd1:4.2.1](), [an1.248:1.1]()).The commentary says this phrase refers to two individual named Vassa and Bhañña from the country of Ukkalā (Sanskrit _oḍra_, modern Odisha). But this seems quite unlikely. Ukkalā was distant and largely unknown, mentioned only once elsewhere in the Pali canon ([pli-tv-kd1:4.2.1]()). These teachers with their odd names (“Rain” and “Speak”) appear nowhere else. Yet they are referred to as if they were well known, as indicated by the phrase _yepi te ahesuṁ_, elsewhere used only of “those who were Buddhas of the past”. There seems no reason the Buddha should abruptly allude to such obscure figures as if they were an authority. Perhaps read _ukkalā_ from root _kal_ (“to sound”) with prefix _ud_ (“up”), “with raised voice”, cf. Sanskrit _kalabhāṣin_ (“with pleasing voice”). Then _vassa_ from _vṛṣa_ (“bull, chief”), for which compare the expression, _uḷārā āsabhī vācā bhāsitā_, “spoke a lofty bull’s word”, i.e. made a proud and dramatic statement. _Bhañña_ is used elsewhere of speaking “out of faith” (_pasādabhañña_, [pli-tv-bu-vb-pj4:8.11.8]()) or of the intoned recitation used for Buddhist texts (_sarabhañña_, [ud5.6:18.2]() = [pli-tv-kd15:3.2.1](), [pli-tv-kd15:3.2.1](), [pli-tv-kd22:1.10.5]()). Thus the sense would be, “those who proudly declaim”.
